newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Zagrebacka to boost housing loans in '97.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Zagrebacka to boost housing loans in '97.

text.p: Croatia's leading bank Zagrebacka Banka said on Monday it would boost housing loans on the back of an expected 400 million German marks rise in hard currency savings in 1997.
"We plan an increase (in housing loans) by some 170 million marks. But this amount could be larger if the citizens' needs are higher," board member Neda Saric told a news conference.
She said Zagrebacka also counted on cheaper foreign funds once it gets a credit rating, which would be channelled into new loans to its clients.
Croatian commercial banks have an obligation to deposit 45 percent of all foreign currency savings abroad.
Director of the bank's retail sector, Zvonimir Jurjevic, said housing loans were the least risky of all bank's placements, with under one percent going uncollected.
The risk with citizens' cash loans was about double that but they were still among Zagrebacka's best business.
Thanks to an increase in currency deposits to 1.45 billion marks, the bank has this year granted citizens 104 million marks for the purchase and refurbishment of houses and flats.
The loans are repayable monthly over 15 years at a fixed annual interest rate of 9.0 percent. Borrowers have to mortgage another property, not the one they are buying.
Although Saric said there would be no lengthening the repayment period or cut in the interest, but the rate would be variable from next year.
Zagrebacka also plans to make other requirements easier. A mandatory deposit, taken as security, will be cut to 10 from between 30 and 50 percent and mortgage terms will be better.
